newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa banks seek help to avert rate hike - paper.
newsitem.headline: South Africa banks seek help to avert rate hike - paper.

text.p: South Africa's leading commercial banks have appealed to the Reserve Bank to help avert an increase in prime overdraft rates by easing pressure in the money market, Business Day newspaper reported on Monday.
Chris Stals, the governor of the central bank, said there had been informal discussions with the banks on the squeeze in the money market but the Bank was not looking to pump cash into the market.

"My message to the banks is quite simply that the pressure will ease when they cut back on credit extension. Any action we might take to help them now will not change the liquidity situation. Only they can do that by curbing their lending," he said.
Stals said the banks' main problem was a shortage of liquid assets, and the Bank was looking at ways to facilitate their access to these assets.
The Bank was considering helping the banks gain access to the assets of the Public Investment Commissioners (PIC), the government's pension fund investment manager, he said.
The banks would sell long-term stock to the PIC in exchange for short-term assets at market-related rates.
Commercial banks are required by law to hold a certain percentage of liquid assets on their balance sheets.

In addition, they need liquid assets as collateral for overnight loans from the central bank when they run out of cash -- a particularly acute demand at present with the daily money market shortage running at close to 10 billion rand.
